name: Sonnet concentrated AI/technology
strategy: Cross-sector momentum/relative-value book, long confirmed sector breakouts (biotech, regional banks) and short confirmed breakdowns (long-duration Treasuries), deliberately avoiding AI/semis so this book expresses a different macro/rotation view than the Round 2 concentrated-AI book.
reassessment_note: This week's tape confirmed all three current legs rather than breaking any of them, so I am adding exposure out of the 38% cash pile instead of replacing names. XBI is up on the week and biotech is getting a fresh catalyst narrative (Merck-Moderna cancer-vaccine breakthrough, 'biotech may be the next breakout trade' coverage) on top of a +35% YTD move -- sizing up. KRE is up on the week and sitting near its 52-week high with an 18.3% trailing total return -- regional-bank momentum is intact, sizing up. TLT's short thesis got direct macro confirmation: the August jobs report beat (162k) revived Fed rate-hike chatter instead of cut hopes, a NY Fed official flagged yields 'near 5%' as a sign of strength not stress, and TLT fell for the week -- adding to the short. I explicitly checked the two other legs named in this book's strategy of record (short gold miners, short crypto weakness) and both are going the wrong way to add: gold/GDX is rallying on central-bank buying with spot near $4,400 and GDX up 53% over the trailing year, and BTC remains up double digits over both rounds' inception windows, so I am leaving both out rather than force a short into strength -- discipline says only add shorts on confirmed breakdowns, and neither is breaking down. Cash comes down from 38% to 20% to reflect that idle cash was the biggest drag on this book relative to SPY.

positions.thesis: Biotech breakout is confirming with fresh catalyst flow (Merck-Moderna cancer-vaccine news) and sector-rotation coverage calling it out as the next breakout trade, on top of a +35% YTD run; up on the week while the broader tape was soft on the jobs print. Adding to the largest position in the book to lean into confirmed sector strength.

Regional banks are near 52-week highs with an 18.3% trailing total return and were up again this week even as headline indices dipped on the jobs report -- a steady/rising-rate backdrop that keeps net interest margins intact is a tailwind for this group, not a headwind. Sizing up on confirmed relative strength.

The August jobs beat (162k, above expectations) flipped the narrative from rate cuts to rate-hike risk, a NY Fed official is framing ~5% yields as a sign of economic strength, and TLT fell on the week -- the long-bond short is the most directly confirmed macro thesis in the book this week. Adding modestly with a tight 6% stop given how sharply rate expectations can reverse on the next data print.
